bib.title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models. Wenhao Yu, Hongming Zhang, Xiaoman Pan, Peixin Cao, Kaixin Ma, Jian Li, Hongwei Wang, Dong Yu (Tencent AI Lab). EMNLP 2024 (arXiv 2311.09210v2, 3 Oct 2024; first posted 2023).

COVERAGE: 57,294 of 57,294 chars read, including limitations, appendix A.1-A.7 and Table 6. The reference list was only skimmed. Figures were not rendered, but the caption text came through the extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: With LLaMa-2 7B and only noisy retrieved documents (100% noise), Chain-of-Note (CoN) lifts the 3-dataset average EM by about 7.9 over plain Retrieve-Read.
  number: +7.94 EM average (NQ +7.55, TriviaQA +9.00, WebQ +7.27)
  setup: LLaMa-2 7B fine-tuned on 10K GPT-4 notes from NQ. DPR on Wikipedia, top-5. Subsets keep only questions where DPR retrieved a gold document. Table 3 (NQ 34.28 to 41.83 EM).
  quote: "An average improvement of +7.9 in EM score on fully noisy documents is observed on three open-domain QA datasets, in average."
  where: Sec 3.3 and Table 3, around char 28,000.
- claim: At 100% noise, both plain RALM and CoN fall below the no-retrieval fine-tuned model, which means irrelevant documents mislead the reader. CoN gets close to the no-retrieval baseline.
  number: no-retrieval average EM 35.98 (Table 2) vs Retrieve-Read 39.72 and CoN 47.66 at 100% noise (Table 3)
  setup: LLaMa-2 7B. The paper's own statement is below. Note the Table 2 and Table 3 numbers come from different eval sets (full test set vs subset). The numbers I cite do not cleanly support "underperformed the no-retrieval setting", so check this before citing.
  quote: "when faced with entirely noisy documents, both the standard RALM and our Chain-of-Note enhanced RALM underperformed compared to the no-retrieval setting. This suggests that RALMs can be misled by noisy information, leading to more hallucinations."
  where: Sec 3.3
- claim: The CoN gain shrinks as noise falls. It is +3.18 EM average at 80% noise, then +2.20, +2.07 and +2.78 at 60%, 40% and 20%, and +2.72 at 0% noise. TriviaQA is roughly flat at low noise (+0.18 EM at 0%, F1 -0.50).
  number: see list
  setup: LLaMa-2 7B, Table 3, noise ratio r means k·r noisy docs among k (e.g. 20% noise with top-5 gives 4 relevant and 1 irrelevant).
  quote: "Experiments with lower noise ratios also consistently demonstrate the improvements brought by CON, aligning the overall QA performance."
  where: Table 3 and Sec 3.3
- claim: CoN raises the rejection rate on out-of-scope real-time questions by 6.9 points absolute (6.1 to 13.0), while EM and F1 barely move. The text's "+10.5" does not match the table.
  number: RR 6.1 to 13.0; EM 15.6 to 15.7; F1 19.9 to 20.3
  setup: LLaMa-2 7B, RealTimeQA questions collected after May 2023 (after the LLaMa-2 pretraining cutoff). RR = rejected questions / total.
  quote: "Retrieve-Read (Shi et al., 2023c) 15.6 19.9 6.1 + CHAIN-OF-NOTE (ours) 15.7 20.3 13.0" and, in the abstract and intro, "a +10.5 increase in the rejection rate for real-time questions"
  where: Table 4, Sec 3.4, intro. Flag: 13.0 minus 6.1 is 6.9, not 10.5 (internal inconsistency in the paper).
- claim: On the full test set (DPR top-k, no controlled noise), the gain is modest. LLaMa-2 7B average EM is 48.49 to 50.46, +1.97.
  number: +1.97 EM avg, +1.81 F1 avg. NQ 47.39 to 48.92, TriviaQA 74.92 to 76.27, WebQ 29.58 to 32.33.
  setup: LLaMa-2 7B fine-tuned. Baseline SAIL (Luo et al., 2023) 45.77 EM avg. QA fine-tune without IR 35.98 EM avg.
  quote: "There is an average improvement of +1.97 in EM scores across all three datasets when using LLaMa-2 as backbone language model."
  where: Sec 3.2, Table 2
- claim: With GPT-4-1106 in zero-shot prompting (no training), CoN beats Chain-of-Thought (CoT) in retrieval-augmented QA, but the margins are small.
  number: Accuracy, in the order of Table 2's four columns: Retrieve-Read 61.8 / 70.6 / 56.8 / 63.1; +CoT 63.6 / 71.2 / 58.4 / 64.4; +CoN 63.8 / 74.6 / 58.8 / 65.7 (average +2.6 over Retrieve-Read). Column order is not preserved in the extraction; the first three are probably NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ and the fourth the average.
  setup: GPT-4-1106. Metric is accuracy (substring match), because EM is unsuitable for GPT-4. Prompts in A.5. Without retrieval, GPT-4 scores 54.0 / 74.2 / 56.2 / 61.5.
  quote: "+ CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT 63.6 71.2 58.4 64.4 + CHAIN-OF-NOTE (OURS) 63.8 74.6 58.8 65.7"
  where: Table 2, Sec 3.3. Caution: on TriviaQA, GPT-4 without retrieval (74.2) matches CoN (74.6) and beats plain Retrieve-Read (70.6).
- claim: Larger models gain less from retrieval, and retrieval can hurt on easy datasets like TriviaQA.
  number: none
  setup: GPT-4 vs LLaMa-2 7B, Table 2.
  quote: "The impact of utilizing retrieval is observed to be less pronounced with larger models and can even be detrimental in certain cases, such as with TriviaQA, where questions are mostly straightforward."
  where: Sec 3.2
- claim: Generating notes is costly. Full CoN takes about 20 times longer to decode (12.02 s vs 0.61 s per example). Hybrid training removes that cost, at slightly lower robustness.
  number: 0.6104 s (Retrieve-Read), 12.0192 s (CoN), 0.6074 s (CoN hybrid), average decoding time per example on 8×A100 GPUs. Figure 3 (EM by noise ratio, NQ), values 100% to 0% noise: standard 34.3, 54.3, 61.4, 64.6, 67.2, 69.2; CoN 41.8, 56.6, 63.4, 65.9, 70.0, 73.3; hybrid 36.3, 55.8, 63.6, 65.2, 70.1, 73.1.
  setup: Hybrid training = 50% of training on standard RALM (no notes) and 50% on CoN, with a distinct prompt prefix for each type. At inference only the standard prompt is used.
  quote: "we allocate 50% of the training time to the standard RALM, which involves directly generating answers without notes, and the other 50% to RALM with CoN."
  where: Sec 2.3.3, Sec 3.5, Table 5, Fig 3
- claim: CoN helps more when DPR fails to retrieve a gold document. On NQ the gain is +1.2 when DPR retrieves relevant documents and +2.3 when it does not.
  number: +1.2 vs +2.3
  setup: NQ, LLaMa-2 7B.
  quote: "the average improvement is +1.2 when DPR retrieves relevant documents and +2.3 when it does not on the NQ dataset."
  where: Sec 3.2

Method details
- For each of k retrieved documents the model writes a reading note, then gives the final answer.
- Three note types: (a) the document answers the question, so answer from it. (b) The document gives context, so combine it with the model's own knowledge to infer the answer. (c) Everything is irrelevant and the model knows nothing, so answer "unknown".
- Training data: 10K questions sampled from NQ train. GPT-4 wrote the notes with instructions plus in-context examples, and quality was checked by human review of "a small subset". LLaMa-2 7B was then fine-tuned with ordinary supervised training.
- Fine-tuning settings: 3 epochs, batch 128, learning rate 5e-6 (swept over 1e-6 to 2e-5), bfloat16, DeepSpeed ZeRO, greedy decoding.
- Retriever: DPR over Wikipedia. Prompts use five passages.
- Dataset stats (Table 1): DPR recall is 73.82 on NQ, 89.95 on TriviaQA and 64.22 on WebQ. Subset sizes are 2,086 of 3,610 (NQ), 7,074 of 7,993 (TriviaQA) and 1,231 of 2,032 (WebQ).
- Case studies (Table 6): the last US Summer Olympics (plain RALM answered 2016, CoN answered 1996), and the language of the first Jnanpith recipient (plain RALM answered "G. Sankara Kurup", CoN answered Malayalam, by combining two passages).

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "One major limitation of the Chain-of-Note (CoN) approach is its increased inference cost due to the sequential generation of notes." Note quality also varies with the complexity of the retrieved documents.
- Not shown: only one trained model size (LLaMa-2 7B), and GPT-4 only zero-shot. Training notes come from NQ only. The retriever is DPR only, and the corpus is Wikipedia.
- Noise is synthetic. The mix of gold and irrelevant documents is built by hand, and questions with no gold document in DPR's results are excluded from the robustness subsets.
- Only a small human check of GPT-4 note quality; no significance tests or multiple seeds are reported.
- Unknown-robustness is tested on RealTimeQA only. The rejection rate rises, but EM and F1 are flat, and the paper does not measure false refusals on answerable questions.
- Dated: the model is LLaMa-2 7B and the reader is GPT-4-1106. EM scores are low compared with later systems.
- Hybrid training: the paper shows only the NQ curve (Fig 3) and a timing table. There are no per-dataset numbers for hybrid.

BUILDS ON
- Chain-of-Thought: Wei et al., 2022; Kojima et al., 2022.
- Retrieve-then-read RALMs: Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG); Guu et al., 2020 (REALM); Izacard and Grave, 2021 (FiD); Karpukhin et al., 2020 (DPR); Shi et al., 2023c; Lazaridou et al., 2022.
- Irrelevant-context studies: Shi et al., 2023a (LLMs are easily distracted by irrelevant context); Creswell et al., 2022 (Selection-Inference); Mallen et al., 2023 (when not to trust LMs).
- Closest prior work, training a RALM to ignore irrelevant context: Yoran et al., 2023.
- SAIL baseline: Luo et al., 2023.
- Related chain-of-X work: Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al., 2023); IR-CoT (Trivedi et al., 2023).
- Datasets: Kwiatkowski et al., 2019 (NQ); Joshi et al., 2017 (TriviaQA); Berant et al., 2013 (WebQ); Kasai et al., 2023 (RealTimeQA).

CODE: no code. The CoN prompt is in A.5 and is worth keeping verbatim:
"Task Description: 1. Read the given question and five Wikipedia passages to gather relevant information. 2. Write reading notes summarizing the key points from these passages. 3. Discuss the relevance of the given question and Wikipedia passages. 4. If some passages are relevant to the given question, provide a brief answer based on the passages. 5. If no passage is relevant, direcly provide answer without considering the passages."
The CoT baseline prompt is "Task Description: Think step by step to answer the question." The plain RALM prompt is "Task Description: The primary objective is to briefly answer the question."
The RALM formula is p(y|x) = Σ_i p(y|d_i, x) p(d_i|x), summed over the top-k documents (Sec 2.2).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): RALM with and without CoN on the "It Must Have Been Love" question. It shows the failure and the note-based fix in one picture.
- Fig 2 (p3): the three note types, (a) relevant so find the answer, (b) irrelevant so infer the answer, (c) irrelevant so answer unknown. This is the clearest summary of the method.
- Fig 3 (p6): EM vs noise ratio for standard, CoN and hybrid on NQ.
- Table 6 (appendix): the two case studies.

PROBLEMS: Table columns in Table 2's GPT-4 block lost their header alignment in the extraction, so the column mapping for GPT-4 is inferred. The RealTimeQA "+10.5" rejection-rate gain in the text conflicts with the Table 4 values (13.0 minus 6.1 is 6.9), so cite the table. The paper's wording that CoN "performs nearly as well as" the no-retrieval baseline at 100% noise is not clearly supported by the numbers I could compare, because Table 2 and Table 3 use different eval sets.
